arxiv-1912-13154.title: Implicit regularization and momentum algorithms in nonlinearly parameterized adaptive control and prediction
arxiv-1912-13154.creator: Nicholas M. Boffi, Jean-Jacques E. Slotine
arxiv-1912-13154.description: Abstract Stable concurrent learning and control of dynamical systems is the subject of adaptive control. Despite being an established field with many practical applications and a rich theory, much of the development in adaptive control for nonlinear systems revolves around a few key algorithms.

arxiv-2105-03172.title: Reward prediction for representation learning and reward shaping
arxiv-2105-03172.creator: Hlynur Davíð Hlynsson, Laurenz Wiskott
arxiv-2105-03172.description: Abstract One of the fundamental challenges in reinforcement learning (RL) is the one of data efficiency: modern algorithms require a very large number of training samples, especially compared to humans, for solving environments with high-dimensional observations. The severity of this problem is increased when the reward signal is sparse.

arxiv-2106-13725.title: The clustering of galaxies in the completed SDSS-IV extended Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey: Primordial non-Gaussianity in Fourier Space 2021 The clustering of galaxies in the completed SDSS-IV extended Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey: Primordial non-Gaussianity in Fourier Space – R
arxiv-2106-13725.creator: Eva-Maria Mueller, Mehdi Rezaie, Will J. Percival, Ashley J. Ross, Rossana Ruggeri, Hee-Jong Seo, Héctor Gil-Marín, Julian Bautista, Joel R. Brownstein, Kyle Dawson, Axel de la Macorra, Nathalie Palanque-Delabrouille, Graziano Rossi, Donald P. Schneider, Christophe Yèche
arxiv-2106-13725.description: Abstract We present measurements of the local primordial non-Gaussianity parameter f NL local f_{\mathrm{NL}}^{\mathrm{local}}\ from the clustering of 343,708 quasars with redshifts 0.8 < z < 2.2 distributed over 4808 square degrees from the final data release (DR16) of the extended Baryon acoustic Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey (eBOSS), the largest volume spectroscopic survey up to date.

arxiv-2106-14643.title: Privacy-Utility Trade-Offs Against Limited Adversaries
arxiv-2106-14643.creator: Xiaoming Duan, Zhe Xu, Rui Yan, Ufuk Topcu
arxiv-2106-14643.description: Abstract We study privacy-utility trade-offs where users share privacy-correlated useful information with a service provider to obtain some utility. The service provider is adversarial in the sense that it can infer the users’ private information based on the shared useful information.

arxiv-2110-08052.title: Dynamical IP ⋆ -sets in weak rings
arxiv-2110-08052.creator: Pintu Debnath, Sayan Goswami
arxiv-2110-08052.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Pintu Debnath, Sayan Goswami. Hindman in [ 1 ] , proved that IP ⋆ - sets contain all possible finite sums and products of a sum subsystem of any sequence in ℕ \mathbb{N} . In a recent work [ 3 ] , the second author of this article has proved that a stronger result holds for dynamical IP ⋆ - sets. In this article we will establish a non-commutative version of this result.

arxiv-2310-11913.title: Deterministic Sparse Pattern Matching via the Baur-Strassen Theorem
arxiv-2310-11913.creator: Nick Fischer
arxiv-2310-11913.description: Abstract How fast can you test whether a constellation of stars appears in the night sky? This question can be modeled as the computational problem of testing whether a set of points P P can be moved into (or close to) another set Q Q under some prescribed group of transformations.

arxiv-2508-05746.title: Can dynamic dark energy explain the S 8 S_{8} tension, the ‘lensing is low’ effect, or strong baryon feedback?
arxiv-2508-05746.creator: S. Heydenreich 1, A. Leauthaud 1, J. DeRose 2
arxiv-2508-05746.description: Abstract We investigate the impact of a DESI motivated dynamic dark energy cosmology on three cosmological anomalies, the S 8 S_{8} tension, the ‘lensing is low’ effect, and observations of strong baryonic feedback. We analyze how these observations vary in Λ \Lambda CDM versus dynamic dark energy.

arxiv-2508-12117.title: SPIDER: Scalable Probabilistic Inference for Differential Earthquake Relocation
arxiv-2508-12117.creator: Zachary E. Ross, John D. Wilding, Kamyar Azizzadenesheli, Aitaro Kato
arxiv-2508-12117.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Zachary E. Ross, John D. Wilding, Kamyar Azizzadenesheli, Aitaro Kato. Seismicity catalogs are larger than ever due to an explosion of techniques for enhanced earthquake detection and an abundance of high-quality datasets. Bayesian inference is a popular framework for locating earthquakes due to its ability to propagate and quantify uncertainty into the inversion results, but traditional methods do not scale well to high-dimensional parameter spaces, making them unsuitable for double-difference relocation where the number of parameters can reach the millions.

arxiv-2510-06915.title: LongRM: Revealing and Unlocking the Context Boundary of Reward Modeling
arxiv-2510-06915.creator: Zecheng Tang 1,2 , Baibei Ji 1,2 , Quantong Qiu 1,2 , Haitian Wang 1,2 , Xiaobo Liang 1 Juntao Li 1,2 , Min Zhang 1 and 1 Soochow University 2 LCM Laboratory and {zctang, bbji}@stu.suda.edu.cn {ljt, minzhang}@suda.edu.cn
arxiv-2510-06915.description: Abstract Reward model (RM) plays a pivotal role in aligning large language model (LLM) with human preferences. As real-world applications increasingly involve long history trajectories, e.g., LLM agent, it becomes indispensable to evaluate whether a model’s responses are not only high-quality but also grounded in and consistent with the provided context.

arxiv-2512-19193.title: The IXPE and multifrequency polarimetric view of the extreme blazars 1ES 1101-232 and RGB J0710+591
arxiv-2512-19193.creator: Fabrizio Tavecchio, Dawoon E. Kim, Gabriel Emery, Ioannis Liodakis, Iván Agudo, Paolo Coppi, Giampiero Tagliaferri, Laura Di Gesu, Tullia Sbarrato, Lucia Ballo, Alberto Sciaccaluga, Steven R. Ehlert, Giacomo Bonnoli, Francisco José Aceituno, Carolina Casadio Víctor Casanova, Immacolata Donnarumma, J
arxiv-2512-19193.description: Abstract Multiwavelength polarimetry is a powerful tool to probe magnetic field and flow geometries in the relativistic jets of blazars. In this respect, particularly interesting are the sources whose synchrotron emission covers a broad range of frequencies, from radio to X-rays, such as the BL Lac objects of the HSP type.

arxiv-2601-22156.title: Hybrid Linear Attention Done Right: Efficient Distillation and Effective Architectures for Extremely Long Contexts
arxiv-2601-22156.creator: Yingfa Chen, Zhen Leng Thai, Zihan Zhou, Zhu Zhang, Xingyu Shen, Shuo Wang, Chaojun Xiao, Xu Han, Zhiyuan Liu
arxiv-2601-22156.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Yingfa Chen, Zhen Leng Thai, Zihan Zhou, Zhu Zhang, Xingyu Shen, Shuo Wang, Chaojun Xiao, Xu Han, Zhiyuan Liu. Hybrid Transformer architectures, which combine softmax attention blocks and recurrent neural networks (RNNs), have shown a desirable performance-throughput tradeoff for long-context modeling, but their adoption and studies are hindered by the prohibitive cost of large-scale pre-training from scratch. Some recent studies have shown that pre-trained softmax attention blocks can be converted into RNN blocks through parameter transfer and knowledge distillation.

pmc-10735514.title: FIVE BIODEMOGRAPHIC PRINCIPLES OF AGING THAT EMERGED FROM RESEARCH ON THE MEDITERRANEAN FRUIT FLY
pmc-10735514.creator: James Carey
pmc-10735514.description: Because of its large size, visually-distinct sex differences, abundance in the wild and ease of rearing at both industrial and individual levels, the Mediterranean fruit fly (medfly) is an ideal model organism for conducting research on the demography of aging.

pmc-11371700.title: Identification of TIMP1-induced dysregulation of epithelial-mesenchymal transition as a key pathway in inflammatory bowel disease and small intestinal neuroendocrine tumors shared pathogenesis
pmc-11371700.creator: Minh Tuan Tran
pmc-11371700.description: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) is believed to be a risk factor for Small Intestinal Neuroendocrine Tumors (SI-NET) development; however, the molecular relationship between IBD and SI-NET has yet to be elucidated. In this study, we use a systems biology approach to uncover such relationships.

pmc-11436780.title: Towards geospatially-resolved public-health surveillance via wastewater sequencing
pmc-11436780.creator: Braden T Tierney, Jonathan Foox, Krista A Ryon, Daniel Butler, Namita Damle, Benjamin G Young, Christopher Mozsary, Kristina M Babler, Xue Yin, Yamina Carattini, David Andrews, Alexander G Lucaci, Natasha Schaefer Solle, Naresh Kumar, Bhavarth Shukla, Dušica Vidović, Benjamin Currall, Sion L William
pmc-11436780.description: Wastewater is a geospatially- and temporally-linked microbial fingerprint of a given population, making it a potentially valuable tool for tracking public health across locales and time. Here, we integrate targeted and bulk RNA sequencing (N = 2238 samples) to track the viral, bacterial, and functional content over geospatially distinct areas within Miami Dade County, USA, from 2020-2022.

pmc-11690287.title: SOCIAL INVISIBILITY OF ELDER ABUSE IN FAMILIES: A PHENOMENON IN PHILIPPINE SOCIETY
pmc-11690287.creator: Carmelina Oyales, Victoria Apuan, Ronaldo Motilla
pmc-11690287.description: In a country where the prevailing culture puts a premium on respect and care for the elderly, elder abuse is an interesting phenomenon. The study focuses on elder abuse and the different forms of abuse occurring in Filipino communities. A qualitative study composed of individual interviews of 10 victims of elder abuse were undertaken.

pmc-13026462.title: Liberation from Non-Invasive Ventilation in Complex Intensive Care Unit Patients
pmc-13026462.creator: Hafsa Safdar, Joseph B. Barney
pmc-13026462.description: The evolution of non-invasive mechanical ventilation (NIV) from the iron lung of the 1950s to the use of sophisticated ventilators with mask apparatus has allowed for the optimal management of a wide range of respiratory disorders. NIV is now a mainstay in the management of acute, chronic and acute-on-chronic hypoxemic and hypercapnic respiratory failure from diverse etiologies.

pmc-13428819.title: Carrying Strength and Silence: A Patient Perspective on Postpartum Mood in Black Motherhood
pmc-13428819.creator: Amber Nelson-Fuller

pmc-13554842.title: Enumeration Class of Polyominoes Inscribed in James Abacus and Related ECO
pmc-13554842.creator: Eman F. Mohommed, jalal Abd Jassim, Alina Alb Lupas, Ali A. Aubad, Eman Mohommed, Hayder R. Hashim, Hayder R. Hashim, Eman Mohommed, Ayesha Qureshi
pmc-13554842.description: This paper studies a class of polyominoes. The new class is defined through a representation on the James abacus through nested chain which denoted Ω -nested Abacus. Depended on partition, beta number, nested chain we defined the structural condition this class. A local transformations, called SSPT-transformation and MSPT-transformation are formulated on the even chains.
